text.title: Agent Invocation Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules constraining the invocation config for a research subagent: the tool allowlist, the pair of termination controls, caller-side output validation, sequencing against shared search quota, forced citation, context isolation on return, and the trace fields that make a run diagnosable afterwards.

rule.statement: `tools_whitelist` MUST enumerate the exact tools granted. A research subagent gets Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch and nothing else; if it must persist output it gets Write scoped to the one path declared in `trace_contract`. Bash, Edit and unscoped Write are forbidden.

rationale.source: Claude Code subagent definition — `tools` frontmatter field

rule.rationale: Omitting the field makes the subagent inherit the parent's full toolset. An unbounded research agent that can run shell will "helpfully" reorganize files or install a package mid-run, and the damage surfaces later as an unexplained working-tree diff rather than as an agent error anyone traces back.

rule.statement: `max_iterations` MUST be a positive integer AND the config MUST declare an explicit stop condition (output validates against `output_schema`, or no new source URL in the last two tool calls). Neither may be omitted in favour of the other.
rule.rationale: A cap without a stop condition means the agent exhausts the budget and returns whatever partial state it held at the last turn — which parses as a normal answer downstream. A stop condition without a cap means a search loop that keeps finding "one more source" runs until the session limit.

rule.statement: The caller MUST validate the returned payload against `output_schema` before consuming it, and treat a violation as a retry with the violation echoed back — never as a field to patch, default or regex out.

rationale.source: Structured-output failure modes in long generations

rule.rationale: Models emit nearly-correct JSON: under a long generation a required field is silently dropped rather than malformed. A caller that repairs the shape locally propagates the omission as a legitimate empty value, and the gap appears three stages later as a conclusion drawn from nothing.

rule.statement: Invocations that share one search provider (Brave, Tavily, Perplexity, the built-in WebSearch quota) MUST run sequentially, with each stage passing the previous stage's output path in its prompt. Parallel fan-out over a shared provider is forbidden in the config.

rationale.source: agent-integration.md in this methodology directory — faion-researcher constraints

rule.rationale: Parallel research stages issue overlapping queries against one key: the quota is consumed twice for the same answers and the provider starts rate-limiting mid-run, so some stages return degraded results while others return full ones and the difference is invisible in the merged report.

rule.statement: The subagent prompt MUST forbid estimation and require every external figure to carry a URL the agent itself fetched; where no source exists the agent writes the literal string "Data not available". A figure with no URL fails caller-side validation.

rationale.source: agent-integration.md — hallucinated sources in research modes

rule.rationale: Without forced citation models generate plausible review-site slugs and vendor pricing pages that do not exist. Because a fabricated citation is formatted exactly like a real one, no downstream reader can distinguish them, and the fabrication is laundered into every artefact that quotes the report.

rule.statement: When expected output exceeds roughly a few thousand tokens, the subagent MUST write to the declared path and return only that path plus a short summary. Returning raw search results or full transcripts to the parent is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Subagent invocation exists to keep tool noise out of the parent window. Returning the payload puts it back, so a nine-stage research run leaves the orchestrator with no room to actually orchestrate — the cost of the isolation is paid without receiving the benefit.

rule.statement: `trace_contract` MUST declare the log field names and a storage path, and the field set MUST include `invocation_id`, `iterations_used`, `stop_reason` and `tools_called`.
rule.rationale: Without `stop_reason` and `iterations_used` a run truncated at the cap is indistinguishable, after the fact, from a run that finished — both produce an output file. Every later question about why a report is thin then requires re-running the agent instead of reading the trace.
